items.title: Joe Bushkin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: I was there with Milt Hinton, Buck Clayton, Jo Jones on drums, that was the quartet

ctx.x: And you played mostly for dancing at these ballrooms?

Yeah it was back in the 30’s, the early 30’s, and into the swing era. And I played intermission piano at Kelly’s Stables when the Coleman Hawkins Quartet was there, and I was at the Embers. I could go on endlessly, where — we opened the Embers in New York which became the hot jazz venue and we were there for nine weeks and believe it or not I was there with Milt Hinton, Buck Clayton, Jo Jones on drums, that was the quartet, and Art Tatum was there appearing.
Did you guys play one set?

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I didn't find out until I went out with Joe Bushkin what I knew about Fess.

ctx.x: I didn't find out until I went out with Joe Bushkin what I knew about Fess. I've been there, you see. Because I was a kid, I was a kid that just wanted to be around you.

You're just amazing. Just a minute, Jo, I want to get back to something else. I want to ask you - it turns out as time will show and has shown as of 1973, in all the annals of band playing dance music, there's only been one superlative rhythm section, one that was impeccable, that is held in esteem by every jazz musician in the world and every jazz listener, everyone that appreciates jazz, and that was the great rhythm section which you headed in the Count Basie band. That is with you, Jo Jones, on drums; Walter…
